- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid false rebounds.  
- After a strong price spike (forecast > 10% above recent 7-day average), apply a 3–5 day mean reversion bias downward.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.75) and forecast diverges from history, favor the 14-day moving average over 30-day forecast.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast (especially in first 7 days), apply a 2–3% downward adjustment to next period’s forecast.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 1–3% per week to reflect downward drift.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by > 3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.0% per day from future forecasts.
